text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English Quaker leader WILLIAM PENN was born in 1644. He founded the American Quaker colony of Pennsylvania.

American-born Irish politician EAMON DE VALERA, who was president of the Irish Republic from 1919 to 1922, was born in 1882. He was Irish prime minister three times and subsequently president from 1959 to 1973.
American military commander DWIGHT D. EISENHOWER was born in 1890. He was in charge of the Allied invasion of Europe in World War Two and twice president of the United States after the war.
American silent film heroine LILLIAN GISH was born in 1896.

British singer CLIFF RICHARD (HARRY WEBB), who has had top selling hits since the fifties, was born in 1940. His first hit was "Move It" (1958). Others include "Living Doll" in 1959 and another version in 1986, "Summer Holiday" (1963), "Devil Woman" (1976), "We Don't Talk Anymore" (1979) and "Dreamin'" (1980).

British singer, pianist, guitarist and songwriter JUSTIN HAYWARD, who joined the 'Moody Blues' in 1967, was born in 1946. Hits included "Nights in White Satin" (1967), "Your Wildest Dreams" (1986) and "I Know You're Out There Somewhere" (1988).
** EVENTS **
1791 : The Society of United Irishmen was set up in
Belfast to demand rights for Catholics.
1912 : United States president THEODORE ROOSEVELT was
shot in an attempted assassination.
1913 : Britain's worst mining disaster claimed 439 lives
in an explosion at Universal Colliery in South Wales. An explosion at the same pit 13 years earlier had claimed the lives of 83 miners.
1922 : The last turf was laid on the playing field of the
Imperial Stadium at Wembley in London.
1923 : Severe flooding inundated Melbourne and many parts
of Victoria. The Yarra Burst its banks and drowned a youth canoeing at Abbotsford and swept away a baby girl at Flemington. 1944 : The "desert fox" Germany's Field Marshall ERWIN ROMMEL

died. Heart failure was said to be the cause however some sources believed ROMMEL had poisoned himself. HITLER had made it known that he was aware of ROMMEL's involvement in his assassination plot and that ROMMEL was to be brought to trial. Other plotters had been put to death by slow hanging from anoose of piano wire suspended from a meat-hook. ROMMEL commanded the Afrika Corps with distinction during the North African campaign from 1941 to 1943. ROMMEL was 53.
1959 : Hollywood idol Australian-born ERROL FLYNN died at

the age of 50. He made his first film with CHARLES CHAUVEL in 1933 "In the Wake of the Bounty". He made a name as Captain Blood and Robin Hood. His hell-raising ways landed him in court or in the gossip columns for seducing under-age girls and involvement in night club brawls.
1968 : An earthquake measuring 6.9 on the Richter Scale
almost destroyed the Western Australian town of Meckering.
1977 : American entertainer BING CROSBY collapsed and

died of a heart attack. He had just completed a round of golf near Madrid. He was 73. In 1940 he began his long association with the "Road films" and co-stars BOB HOPE and DOROTHY LAMOUR. One of his most successful and *nduring films was "High Society", with GRACE KELLY and FRANK SINATRA.
1985 : Brisbane businessman BRIAN JAMES MAHER was jailed
for five years for bottom-of-the-harbour tax avoidance.
1988 : An article in London's "Times" revealed that

NAPOLEON could have been killed by his wallpaper. He had high levels of arsenic in his blood when he died and this led to suspicions of poisoning. Research showed that the wallpaper in his room contained arsenic in the printing ink and if a damp fungus had developed on the paper the arsenic would have been released into the air.
1991 : The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Burma's

opposition leader AUNG SAN SUU KYI. The daughter of the father of Burmese independence GENERAL AUNG SAN returned to the country in 1988 and formed an opposition party to fight the military government. In 1989 she was put under house arrest and banned from taking part in the 1990 elections. The Nobel Peace Prize seen as part of an international effort to gain her release.
